findings.evidence: On 0e9a51ea: has_link_or_contact('refunds-portal \u0628\u0650\u065c shop') == False (also '\u0628\u0650\u065c\u0655 shop', '\u0621\u0650\u065c\u0655 shop', '\u0915\u093c\u0901\u0902 shop', '\u0915\u0901\u0902 shop', '\u0e01\u0e31\u0e48\u0e4c shop', '\u0628\u0650\u065c\u0655 cash'), and mask_links returns the text unchanged; the bare letter ('refunds-portal \u0628 shop', '\u0915 shop') and one letter + one mark ('\u0628\u0650') are detected. With SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.': SY.verify(claim [1], [src]) keeps the claim with its citation, SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline',[src]) keeps the sentence, surface.clean leaves it unmasked and validate._URLISH does not match. Cause: _bare keeps a mark whose script matches its base letter, and _separator_word counts base characters (marks included) as distinct letters: len(base)==1 fails and len(set(base))=3 > _MAX_FOREIGN, so a one-letter word (a D17 separator) becomes the name. D17 says 'at most two distinct letters'; marks are not letters. Probe: /tmp/uri_review_R23/p1.py, p2.py.
findings.suggested_fix: In _separator_word, apply the single-letter and _MAX_FOREIGN tests to the letters only (characters whose category is not M) after _bare, e.g. letters = [c for c in base if unicodedata.category(c)[0] != 'M']; keep base only for the stroke test. Add regression cases for an Arabic, Devanagari and Thai letter plus 2-3 own-script marks before 'shop'/'cash', together with ordinary-text controls ('Cairo (\u0627\u0644\u0642\u0627\u0647\u0631\u0629) is old.').
